LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 10 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we relate events in a book to our own life experiences? 2. How can you predict the information in a book even before you read it?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. preview a text on proper use of leisure time for general understanding,

2. make predictions about events in a text,

3. infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions using prior knowledge and contextual clues,

4. answer direct and inferential questions orally and in writing,

5. summarise the events in the text through retelling,

6. create a password puzzle using the learnt vocabulary. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. preview a text on proper use of leisure time for general understanding,
2. make predictions about events in a text,
3. infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions using prior knowledge and contextual clues,
4. answer direct and inferential questions orally and in writing,
5. summarise the events in the text through retelling,
6. create a password puzzle using the learnt vocabulary. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to learn on their own and complete tasks is developed as they engage in

self-driven tasks by creating a crossword puzzle using the learnt vocabulary.

• Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving: This is developed as the learner creates a crossword puzzle using the

learnt vocabulary.

Values:
Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner acquires discipline by interacting with information from a reading text on

proper use of leisure time.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills (Decision making): The learner is equipped with decision making skills as they preview a text on proper

use of leisure time.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the skills of reading comprehension to the learning of reading skills in Kiswahili.
